beats.say: Januvia, or sitagliptin: which drug class is it?
Look at the ending of sitagliptin. The whole ending, gliptin, not just gli.
The World Health Organization's list of name stems puts sitagliptin under gliptin. A stem points to the related group a drug belongs to.

claims.quote: Stems define the pharmacologically related group to which the INN belongs.
The use of stems in the selection of International Nonproprietary Names (INN) for pharmaceutical substances

beats.say: And Januvia's FDA label says it plainly: Januvia is a dipeptidyl peptidase-4, or DPP-4, inhibitor.

claims.quote: JANUVIA is a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

beats.say: Two more endings help with the wrong answers. Gliflozin drugs are sodium glucose co-transporter inhibitors, and Jardiance, which contains empagliflozin, is an SGLT2 inhibitor. Glitazone drugs are thiazolidinedione derivatives.

claims.quote: -gliflozin (see gli) sodium glucose co-transporter inhibitors, phlorizin derivatives
JARDIANCE tablets for oral use contain empagliflozin, an inhibitor of the SGLT2
JARDIANCE is a sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor
-glitazone (see gli) peroxisome proliferator activating receptor-γ (PPAR-γ) agonists, thiazolidinedione derivatives

beats.say: So: Januvia, sitagliptin, is a DPP-4 inhibitor.

claims.quote: JANUVIA is a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor

notes: Option C (biguanide) is not explained: no saved source names metformin's class.
Stems are a naming target ('Whenever possible'), not a guarantee, and apply to generic names, not brands; the script says 'points to', not 'proves'.
Look-alike names (ISMP: Januvia/Janumet, sitaGLIPtin/SUMAtriptan) are not covered.

ai.verdict: blind answer A, high confidence, matches key
